sources.title: Changes to Clinic Appointments
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: At the Riverside clinic, the front desk has changed its appointment process for the winter. Patients who need another time should call reception at least one day in advance so staff can offer the unused slot to someone else. Anyone arriving with a new prescription should bring the medicine list from their last visit. If a patient cannot attend, the clinic asks them to cancel rather than leave a space empty. On busy mornings, the waiting-room display shows estimated delays; staff update it every thirty minutes. Patients with urgent symptoms should speak directly to reception instead of waiting for a routine appointment.

sources.title: A Temporary Bus Diversion
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: The city transport team will close Market Street to buses from 8 p.m. Friday while crews repair a damaged drainage cover. Route 6 will use Oak Avenue in both directions; the diversion will remain in effect until inspectors confirm the road is safe. Digital signs at three stops will show the temporary route, and drivers will announce the change before leaving the central station. The team will review passenger reports on Monday and adjust the notice if any stop information is unclear. Passengers who need step-free access should check the updated stop map, because two temporary stops have no raised platform.

sources.title: Comparing Coastal Bird Counts
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: A university ecology group is comparing monthly bird counts from two coastal wetlands. Because volunteers used different observation times in the first year, the analyst will account for the length of each visit before comparing totals. The team will also check the new counts against the field log to identify missing entries. Results will be reported separately for each wetland, since the sites differ in vegetation and visitor access. The researchers plan to share the method with local conservation officers so they can repeat the survey next spring. Any estimate that relies on a small number of observations will be described as provisional, not as evidence of a long-term decline.
